parts.name: monk2_model
parts.original_hypothesis: How the parts combine: the five children are added on the logit scale (each exit times its output weight, plus the output bias) and passed through the output sigmoid; a1:1 has no edge and no effect. The training labels follow the MONK-2 rule: the outcome rate is 100% for the 113 training rows where two of the six attributes take their first value and 0% for the other 232. The model learnt a different, looser rule: say yes when a5 is not 1 and one or two of the six attributes take their first value. Over the 432 combinations of the input space this rule agrees with the model's yes/no on 83.8% of cells (25 rule-yes cells the model says no to, 45 the other way), against 64.8% for the training rule. By count of first values, with a5 not 1 the model says yes for 21% of cells with none, 82% with one, 91% with two, 52% with three and 0% with four; with a5=1 it says yes for 0%, 0%, 3%, 0%, 0% and 0% of cells with zero to five other first values. The upper limit comes from many_firsts_gate (three or more first values among a2, a3, a4 and a6) and the a5=1 penalty from direct_terms; a4_not2_bonus adds a flat reward for a4 not 2; a2_3_chain and a1_2_unit are small. The a5=1 penalty is the model's main error: the 87 training rows with a5=1 have an outcome rate of 23.0% but a mean predicted risk of 2.3%. Training performance: AUC 0.766, accuracy 65.5%.
